summary: The rules skill and both annotate commands say the hook annotates line-matched entries automatically and that the agent only handles candidate lists. In fact the hook writes non-closing suggestion tokens that need explicit confirmation.
failure_scenario: The agent runs `gh pr create` and sees 'Suggested 1 entry with (PR-auto: org/repo#9) — pending review, will NOT close on sync'. The rules say the entry was 'annotated automatically' and that its job is 'ONLY the judgment cases', so it does not run `--pick`. The PR merges, sync never closes the entry, and it sits [open] forever. Sync only reports it as 'awaiting confirmation'. The same stale text is in annotate-pr.md and annotate-commit.md, and the rules' Format section also omits the (PR-auto:)/(commit-auto:)/(verified:) tokens.
evidence: SKILL.md:22 'entries whose cited line the diff modifies are annotated automatically and reported in one line. Your job is ONLY the judgment cases the hook surfaces'; annotate-pr.md:59-61 '(`--hook-auto`: line-matched entries annotate silently; exit 3 surfaces candidates)'; annotate-commit.md:45-48 repeats it. Reality: hooks/post-bash-dispatch.sh:250-257 emits 'recorded but NOT closing ... Confirm the ones it genuinely fixes with the --pick command'; lib/annotate.sh:380-383 sets write_annotation=fi_auto_form; CHANGELOG 2.6.0 says the hook text was fixed but not the rules or commands.
suggested_fix: Rewrite the SKILL.md annotation paragraph and the two command files to say hook-inferred annotations are (PR-auto:)/(commit-auto:) suggestions that never close. The agent must run the printed `--pick` for entries the change really fixes. Add the -auto tokens to the Format section.

summary: SessionStart, the rules and annotate-pr.md all tell the agent to run bare `annotate-pr <N>` or `annotate-commit` after a PR or commit. The bare manual path writes the CLOSING (PR:)/(commit:) form on a file-level match with no line check, which can irreversibly false-close.
failure_scenario: Ledger has one [open] entry `lib/foo.sh:900 — unrelated race`. The agent opens a PR that edits lib/foo.sh:12 for something else. SessionStart told it to 'run /found-issues:annotate-pr <N> after opening a PR', and the rules/annotate-pr.md call it the manual fallback. The entry is the sole citer of a touched file, so the bare command writes `(PR: org/repo#N)`, sync flips it to [fixed] on merge, and no command can reopen it. The hook path (--hook-auto) applies a line-overlap check and writes only a suggestion; the manual no-flag path is strictly less safe.
evidence: session-start.sh:464-467 'run `$fi_annotate_pr_ref <N>` after opening a PR ... Sync will auto-flip them when the PR merges'. lib/annotate.sh:380-383 `write_annotation="$annotation"` (canonical unless hook_auto=yes); :493-503 `if [[ "$hook_auto" == "yes" ]] && ! fi_line_matched ... else auto_set+="${cand_lines[$i]}"` so the line check and scope check apply only under hook_auto; :534 writes it.
suggested_fix: Make the SessionStart text, the rules and the manual commands say to always use `--pick <path:line>` after comparing symptoms. Better, have the no-flag manual path compute old_ranges and write the -auto suggestion form too, so only --pick/--all produce a closing token.
needs_runtime_repro: Temp git repo with docs/found-issues.md holding `- [open] 2026-01-01 a.txt:50 — x`. Commit a change to a.txt line 1 on a branch, push, `gh pr create`, then run `found-issues annotate-pr <N>`. Expect `Annotated 1 entry with (PR: ...)` although line 50 was never touched. Then merge and run sync to see [fixed].

summary: fix.md tells the agent to close 'already-fixed' entries with `annotate-commit <sha> --pick`. The v2.4.0 guard rejects any SHA already on the default branch (exit 2) whenever the current branch is not the default, and fix.md never mentions `--force` or requires checking the SHA actually contains the fix.
failure_scenario: An agent verifies an entry as ALREADY-FIXED by commit abc1234, which is on main by definition. It runs `found-issues annotate-commit abc1234 --pick src/x.sh:10` from the fix/found-issues-YYYYMMDD branch and gets exit 2 ('is already on main'). An unattended agent either skips or retries with `--force`, which fix.md never sanctions. With --force there is no check that abc1234 relates to the entry, since the agent may have picked any commit touching the area. Sync's ancestor closer then permanently flips the entry (irreversible false-close risk).
evidence: fix.md:38-40 'If the fixing commit is identifiable, run `found-issues annotate-commit <sha> --pick <path:line>` and sync flips it.' lib/annotate-commands.sh:238-244: `if [[ -n "$default_branch" && "$current_branch" != "$default_branch" ]]; then if git merge-base --is-ancestor ... fi_err "annotate-commit: $short_sha is already on ..."; return 2`.
suggested_fix: In fix.md bucket 1, name `--force` explicitly as required for already-merged SHAs. Require `git show <sha> -- <path>` or `git log -S` evidence that the commit removes the symptom, cited in the PR body. Otherwise route those entries to the sync AI-verify (`resolve`) path.
needs_runtime_repro: On a feature branch of a repo whose main already contains commit C touching a.txt, run `found-issues annotate-commit C --pick a.txt:1`; expect exit 2.

summary: The 'awaiting confirmation' block that sync prints to the agent contradicts the rules. It tells the agent to hand-edit the ledger, prints annotate-commit for PR-auto suggestions too, and its confirm command is rejected by the already-merged guard from a feature branch. sync.md documents none of this output.
failure_scenario: Sync prints '- src/a.sh:3 — suggested (PR-auto: org/repo#9) has merged' followed by 'confirm — found-issues annotate-commit <sha> --pick "<path:line>"'. That is the wrong command for a PR suggestion (it should be annotate-pr). For a landed (commit-auto: sha), running the printed command from any non-default branch exits 2 (guard), so the suggestion stays pending forever. The only 'reject' route offered is 'delete the token by hand', which violates SKILL.md hard rule 1 ('Never write docs/found-issues.md directly'). An agent either hand-edits the ledger or loops.
evidence: sync.sh:403-405 `printf '  confirm  — found-issues annotate-commit <sha> --pick "<path:line>"   (rewrites to the closing form)\n'; printf '  reject   — delete the (commit-auto:/PR-auto:) token from the entry by hand\n'` (printed for both kinds, collected at :128 and :141). annotate-commands.sh:238-244 guard. SKILL.md:47 'Never write docs/found-issues.md directly'. sync.md never mentions the block.
suggested_fix: Print kind-specific confirm commands (annotate-pr <N> --pick for PR-auto; annotate-commit <sha> --force --pick for landed commit-auto). Add a CLI-sanctioned reject path, e.g. an annotate flag or subcommand that strips the -auto token. Document the block in sync.md.
needs_runtime_repro: Ledger entry `- [open] 2026-01-01 a.txt:1 — x (PR-auto: o/r#1)` with PR #1 MERGED (or a commit-auto sha on main), run `found-issues sync` and read the printed block; then run the printed confirm from a feature branch.

summary: Command text and CLI messages tell the agent to remove entries or annotations from the ledger by hand. No CLI verb does either, and both contradict the rules' hard rules 1-2, leaving no sanctioned path.
failure_scenario: The agent decides an entry is a false positive. defer.md says 'those should be removed from the file entirely, not deferred', but SKILL.md hard rule 2 says 'Never delete [open] entries' and rule 1 forbids direct edits. For an entry with a stale (PR: ...) on an abandoned-but-open PR, both `defer` and `resolve` exit 4 saying 'Manually remove the (PR: ...) annotation'. There is no command for that, so the agent hand-edits (bypassing serialization/format guards) or gives up.
evidence: defer.md:29 '**NOT for "this isn't a real issue"**: those should be removed from the file entirely'; defer.md:24 'manually clear the annotation'; lib/defer.sh:133 'Manually remove the (PR: ...) annotation if the PR was abandoned, then re-run defer.'; lib/resolve.sh:131 'remove the annotation first, then re-run resolve.'; SKILL.md:47-48 hard rules 1-2.
suggested_fix: Give false positives a sanctioned closure (e.g. `resolve --verified human` with a note, or a `dismiss` verb). Add a `found-issues unannotate <match>` (or similar) for abandoned PRs. Reword the defer.md bullet and exit-4 messages to point at it.

summary: The branch-delete block message hands the agent the exact bypass (`FOUND_ISSUES_PROMOTE_GUARD=off`), contradicting SKILL.md hard rule 4. Its next-action text is also imprecise: it says to run promote 'on the branch', but promote only works from that branch.
failure_scenario: An unattended or auto-fix agent pruning merged branches hits the block. The message ends with 'To skip this guard for this command only, set FOUND_ISSUES_PROMOTE_GUARD=off.' The cheapest way to finish is that prefix (the hook even parses the inline prefix at :76), so it deletes the branch and the unpromoted [open] entries are lost. A diligent agent instead has to check out the doomed branch to run `found-issues promote`, then follow a 7-step prose procedure it must find in promote.md; the block message names no exact command.
evidence: pre-branch-delete.sh:352-356 'Run /found-issues:promote on the branch first, open a PR ... To skip this guard for this command only, set FOUND_ISSUES_PROMOTE_GUARD=off.'; SKILL.md:51 'Never bypass the pre-branch-delete check — run promote first.'; promote.sh:109-117 requires the current branch to be the non-default branch.
suggested_fix: Drop the bypass sentence from the agent-visible message (keep it in docs/configuration.md for operators). State the concrete sequence: `git checkout <branch> && found-issues promote`, then on a fresh branch off default `found-issues promote --apply --from <branch>`, PR, merge, delete.

summary: `promote` lists and `promote --apply` copies [open] entries by verbatim line equality, while the branch-delete guard compares dedup keys. An entry that main already holds as [fixed], annotated or touched is listed as 'needs promotion', and --apply appends a fresh [open] duplicate to main, resurrecting a closed issue.
failure_scenario: Entry E was logged on main, the feature branch inherited it, and later main's sync flipped E to `[fixed] ... (PR: o/r#5) (fixed: ...)`. The branch still has E as `- [open] ...`. The guard allows deleting the branch (key found on main), but an agent following promote.md Step 1-2 sees E listed as 'not yet on main' and runs `promote --apply --from <branch>`. Line 69 only checks the exact line, so `- [open] <E>` is appended to main's ledger as a duplicate of a [fixed] entry, bumping the open count and eventually re-closing or re-fixing work.
evidence: promote.sh:157 `! printf '%s' "$main_content" | grep -Fxq -- "$line"` and :69 `grep -Fxq -- "$line" "$tmp" && continue` (verbatim only, main's [fixed]/archived variants never match); pre-branch-delete.sh:303-307 builds main_keyset from open|deferred|fixed + archive and :322 compares dedup keys; promote.md:20-27.
suggested_fix: Have promote (list and apply) compare dedup keys against main's ledger plus archive, across all statuses, using the same helper as pre-branch-delete.sh.
needs_runtime_repro: In a temp repo: main ledger holds `- [fixed] 2026-01-01 a.txt:1 — x (verified: ai) (fixed: 2026-02-01)`; a branch has `- [open] 2026-01-01 a.txt:1 — x`. On a chore branch off main run `found-issues promote --apply --from <branch>`; expect 'Applied 1 entry' and a duplicate [open] line.

summary: For unattended dispatch, fix.md has no worktree isolation or clean-tree/base-ref discipline, a per-day branch name that collides on a second run, and `list --json` and the annotate commands can read different ledgers in a worktree.
failure_scenario: An auto-fix dispatcher runs the command in the shared checkout. `Branch fix/found-issues-<YYYYMMDD> off the default branch` has no worktree, no `git fetch`, no check that the tree is clean, and no handling of an existing same-day branch. A second run on the same date fails `checkout -b` or reuses the first run's branch. The ledger is itself a tracked, usually dirty file that rides along onto the fix branch. Phase 1 reads `found-issues list --json`, which searches from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, while annotate-pr/sync search from $PWD. In a worktree whose CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is the main checkout, entries are listed from one ledger and annotated in another; the trailing status line also comes from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.
evidence: fix.md:62-63 'Branch `fix/found-issues-<YYYYMMDD>` off the default branch. Never fix on the current or default branch.'; fix.md:16 `found-issues list --json` (no --cwd). list-status.sh:58 `search_root="${cwd:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}}"` vs annotate-commands.sh:123 `fi_find_issues_file` (default start $PWD, parse-entries.sh:23) and annotate.sh:197 `cmd_status plain` (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR).
suggested_fix: Add a Phase 0: require or enter a dedicated worktree (EnterWorktree or `git worktree add`). `git fetch`, branch from origin/<default>, suffix the branch with time or a counter, refuse on a dirty tree other than the ledger, and pass `--cwd "$PWD"` to every list/status call. Say explicitly that the ledger lives in this worktree.
needs_runtime_repro: From a git worktree whose env has CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<main checkout> and where the two ledgers differ, compare `found-issues list --json` with the file annotate-pr modifies; also run the fix flow twice on one date.

summary: fix.md never commits or pushes the ledger change made by `annotate-pr` after `gh pr create`, and its already-fixed bucket ends in `/found-issues:sync`, which archives. The `(PR:)` annotation never reaches the default branch, and the run leaves uncommitted ledger and archive diffs, the very churn v2.9.1 removed from unattended syncs.
failure_scenario: Phase 4 opens the PR first (the number is needed), then runs `annotate-pr <N> --pick ...`, which rewrites tracked docs/found-issues.md in the working tree only. Nothing says to commit and push that to the PR branch. The PR merges without the annotation, so sync on main has nothing to close and the fixed entries stay [open], while the working tree is left dirty. Separately, bucket 1 says to run `/found-issues:sync` at the end; an explicit sync auto-archives (>30 days or >50 [fixed]), rewriting two tracked files with no commit.
evidence: fix.md:82-88 'Annotate precisely: `found-issues annotate-pr <N> --pick <path:line>` ... NEVER flip ... close via annotate-pr + merge + sync' (no commit/push step); fix.md:40-42 'run `/found-issues:sync` at the end of the run'; sync.sh:426-434 archives on any non-dry-run explicit sync unless FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ARCHIVE=off; CHANGELOG 2.9.1.
suggested_fix: Add a Phase 4 step: after annotate-pr, commit only docs/found-issues.md (`git add` that path, not -A) and push to the PR branch before merge. Run the closing sync as `FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ARCHIVE=off found-issues sync` or `--dry-run`, and say any resulting ledger diff goes in the PR or is reported, never left dirty.

summary: fix.md's allowed-tools covers only a `bats` test runner but the body requires 'the repo's tests + build'. An unattended run on any other stack raises permission prompts. Range entries also cannot be picked from the `path:line` fix.md describes.
failure_scenario: A dispatched run in an npm, pytest or make repo reaches Phase 3 'run the repo's tests + build' and every test command prompts for permission with no operator present, stalling the run. Separately, for an entry located `a.sh:23-49`, `list --json` returns line=23 and line_end=49. fix.md says `--pick <path:line>`, so the agent sends `a.sh:23`, and annotate-pr exits 1 'no [open] entry matches pick'. The picks must be `path:23-49`.
evidence: fix.md:5 `allowed-tools: Bash(found-issues:*), Bash(git:*), Bash(gh:*), Bash(bats:*), Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, Agent`; fix.md:82 `--pick <path:line>`; annotate.sh:43-45 fi_entry_loc renders `path:start-end`, and annotate.sh:124 matches by exact string equality.
suggested_fix: Document that the dispatcher must pre-authorize the repo's test/build commands. Tell the agent to build picks from `raw` or `path:line[-line_end]` exactly as the candidate list prints them.

summary: SessionStart injects 'prepend this italic line to the very top of your next reply' directives (first-run hint, daily statusline nudge) with no headless/entrypoint guard, unlike stop-reminder.sh. In an unattended dispatch they displace the required first line and are consumed by a session no human reads.
failure_scenario: A scheduled or auto-fix run (`claude -p`) starts on a machine whose statusline needs migration. SessionStart injects 'Prepend this single italicized line to the very top of your next reply ... Do not paraphrase.' fix.md requires the final message to open with the scoreboard line `Fixed 9 · ...`, and a downstream parser reading line 1 breaks. The once-ever onboarding marker is also touched by a headless session, so the real operator never sees the hint.
evidence: session-start.sh:96-113 (first-run hint, `touch "$ONBOARD_MARKER"`), :127-192 (statusline nudge, `Prepend this single italicized line to the very top of your next reply`), neither checks CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT; contrast stop-reminder.sh:42-44 `if [[ -n "${CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT:-}" && "${CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT}" != "cli" ]]; then exit 0`; fix.md:92-94 first-line scoreboard.
suggested_fix: Gate both directive blocks on an interactive entrypoint (CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT empty or `cli`) and do not touch the onboarding marker otherwise.
needs_runtime_repro: Run `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-cli bash hooks/session-start.sh </dev/null` with a HOME lacking ~/.claude/found-issues/.onboarded; observe the prepend directive on stdout and the marker created.

summary: The rules demand the found-issues-checked marker on every substantive turn, but the Stop hook only enforces it once per session since 2.8.0. The terse block message has no literal marker string, and the 'full' educational message is effectively unreachable.
failure_scenario: A Claude agent obeys the rules and emits `<!-- found-issues-checked: ... -->` on every substantive turn, though only the first marker-less Stop in a session is ever blocked: wasted output tokens and visible noise per turn. When the one block fires, the stderr is `Stop blocked: missing <!-- found-issues-checked: ... --> marker. (Options: none-noticed | logged | deferred)`. It gives no copy-pasteable string and doesn't say what the options mean. The 'full' form (which has the literal) is only chosen when ~/.claude/found-issues/.onboarded is absent, but SessionStart touches that marker in the very first session before any Stop can fire.
evidence: SKILL.md:34-35 'Every substantive turn includes exactly one HTML comment'; stop-reminder.sh:78-103 once-per-session exit; stop-reminder.sh:234-244 terse form chosen when `.onboarded` exists; session-start.sh:111 `touch "$ONBOARD_MARKER"` (inside the first SessionStart).
suggested_fix: Reword the rule to 'at least once per session, on the first substantive turn that edits or mutates'. Put the exact literal and the three meanings in the terse message.

summary: The Codex path injects the whole rules body, including the Claude-only Stop-hook marker section, though the Stop hook is a no-op on Codex. Several generated Codex skills also tell the agent to use Claude-only tools, and `$ARGUMENTS` becomes a literal placeholder inside a bash fence.
failure_scenario: Every Codex session gets the 'Stop-hook marker (if enabled)' instructions and adds a pointless HTML comment each turn, since stop-reminder.sh exits 0 for Codex. fi-fix tells a Codex agent to 'dispatch parallel read-only subagents (Agent tool)' and fi-sync to 'use the `Read` tool'. fi-setup mentions Claude's `AskUserQuestion`. fi-log's fenced command becomes `found-issues log <the user-provided arguments>`, which an agent may run literally (shell redirection error) instead of substituting a quoted string.
evidence: session-start.sh:65 `awk 'c >= 2 { print } /^---$/ { c++ }'` strips frontmatter only; stop-reminder.sh:46-51 Codex fail-open ('the marker discipline is Claude-only'); codex-skills/fi-fix/SKILL.md:23 'dispatch parallel read-only subagents (Agent tool)'; codex-skills/fi-sync/SKILL.md:48 'use the `Read` tool'; codex-skills/fi-log/SKILL.md:16 `found-issues log <the user-provided arguments>`; lib/codex-rewrite.sh:21 `s|\$ARGUMENTS|<the user-provided arguments>|g`.
suggested_fix: Strip the 'Stop-hook marker' section for harness=codex. Reword tool references neutrally in the source commands ('read the file', 'delegate in parallel if your harness supports it'). Emit `'<arguments>'` as a quoted placeholder or prose, not a bare token in a code block.

summary: log.md (and the annotate/defer templates) splice free-text `$ARGUMENTS` into a bare shell line. The command's own examples contain parentheses, so a literal splice is a bash syntax error, and an apostrophe, backtick or `$(...)` in a symptom breaks or executes. `--critical` is also only honored as the first argument, and the rules don't say so.
failure_scenario: Following the template, the agent runs `found-issues log src/foo.py:42 — null check missing (suggested: add guard before deref)`, which bash rejects with a syntax error near `(`. A symptom like `doesn't escape $(cmd)` or one containing backticks is either an unterminated quote or command substitution of text taken from code or logs. `found-issues log src/a.sh:1 --critical — sym` makes location `src/a.sh:1 --critical`, which does not match the line-spec regexes. It is logged with a spaced pseudo-path and no [!], with no error.
evidence: log.md:17 `found-issues log $ARGUMENTS`; log.md:48 example `... — null check missing (suggested: add guard before deref)`; log.sh:26 `if [[ "${1:-}" == "--critical" ]]` and :38 `local input="$*"`; SKILL.md:14 lists `--critical` after the template without placement.
suggested_fix: Instruct passing the text as one single-quoted argument (escape apostrophes) and `--critical` first: `found-issues log [--critical] '<path:line — symptom (suggested: fix)>'`. Reject `--critical` anywhere else in cmd_log.
needs_runtime_repro: `bash -c "found-issues log src/foo.py:42 — null check missing (suggested: add guard)"` -> syntax error; `found-issues log src/a.sh:1 --critical — test` -> check the logged line.

summary: sync.md hard-codes `found-issues sync` with argument-hint '(no arguments)', so the operator's `--dry-run` (which the Codex description recommends for this irreversible command) is not wired in. The documented summary line also omits most real output.
failure_scenario: The operator, or the Codex skill description's advice ('use --dry-run first when unsure'), runs `/found-issues:sync --dry-run`. The Claude command never passes $ARGUMENTS, so whether the flag reaches the CLI depends on the model, and if not, a full irreversible mutating pass and archive runs. After sync the agent expects only `Synced. Closed: N (P PR + C commit + T tombstone).`, but the CLI also prints 'Dry run', 'Demoted', 'Renamed', 'Synced. Nothing to close.', the status line, the awaiting-confirmation block and an archive block. None of these is described, so the agent skips the actions they imply.
evidence: sync.md:4 `argument-hint: (no arguments)`, :16-18 `found-issues sync`, :32 'The CLI prints a one-line summary: `Synced. Closed: N ...`'; codex-skills/fi-sync description 'use --dry-run first when unsure'; sync.sh:371-406 output variants; sync.sh:46 --dry-run is supported.
suggested_fix: Make sync.md `found-issues sync $ARGUMENTS` with argument-hint `[--dry-run]`, and replace the one-line claim with a short list of the real output sections and what to do for each.

summary: The rules tell the agent to flip entries to the literal string `[fixed] (verified: ai) (fixed: <today>)` but never name `found-issues resolve`, the only sanctioned path. They sit next to the 'never write the ledger directly' rule, and log.md still points at a nonexistent `@found-issues-rules.md`.
failure_scenario: An agent that has only the rules (it saw SessionStart's auto-sync, not sync.md) reads 'flip only fixed → `[fixed] (verified: ai) (fixed: <today>)`'. That is the exact text to hand-write, while hard rule 1 forbids hand-writing. A rule-literal agent either Edits the ledger or does not know how to close. log.md:30 sends the agent to `@found-issues-rules.md`, which the repo's own AGENTS.md says must not exist as an import.
evidence: SKILL.md:26 'flip only fixed → `[fixed] (verified: ai) (fixed: <today>)`'; SKILL.md:47 'Never write docs/found-issues.md directly — commands only.'; lib/resolve.sh:18-25 resolve exists for this; log.md:30 'per the rules in `@found-issues-rules.md`'.
suggested_fix: In SKILL.md Sync, replace the literal with 'close via `found-issues resolve "<fragment>" --verified ai` (never by editing)'. Remove the `@found-issues-rules.md` reference from log.md.

summary: The rules skill carries `disable-model-invocation: true` yet is described as auto-loaded every session on Claude. If Claude Code does not preload such skills, the whole rules surface is inert on Claude, and only Codex injects it, via session-start.
failure_scenario: In a fresh Claude session with the plugin installed, the model never sees the rules (no logging discipline, no --pick rule, no hard rules). Evidence from this session: the skill list includes found-issues:fix, :log, :sync etc. but no found-issues:rules, and no rules text is in context. session-start.sh emits the rules only for harness=codex and says Claude's skill 'injects them'.
evidence: SKILL.md:1-4 frontmatter `disable-model-invocation: true` with description 'Auto-loaded every session by the found-issues plugin'; session-start.sh:37-40 'On Claude Code the skills/rules skill injects them'; hooks/hooks.json and .claude-plugin/plugin.json contain no other injection mechanism.
suggested_fix: Verify the load path on a current Claude Code build. If the flag blocks preloading, remove it, or have SessionStart emit the rules body for Claude too (and dedupe).
needs_runtime_repro: Install the plugin, start a fresh session in a repo with an [open] entry, and ask the model to quote the 'Hard rules' section, or inspect `/context` for the skill. Compare with the same skill minus `disable-model-invocation`.

summary: The per-session injection spends its 15-entry cap on entries the agent can do nothing about (already `(PR:)`-annotated, in flight), and repeats annotation instructions that the rules and hook already carry (and that mislead, see prompt-2).
failure_scenario: A ledger with 20 open entries, 12 of them `(PR: ...)`-annotated, injects up to 15 entries: all criticals plus the newest non-criticals. Most are in-flight lines that crowd out actionable unannotated ones, adding up to a few KB of context every session. The trailing paragraph tells the agent to run annotate-pr/annotate-commit, duplicating SKILL.md:22 and the hook's own post-`gh pr create` message.
evidence: session-start.sh:397-415 builds the fence from crit_entries plus the newest `max_inject` non-criticals with no filter on `(PR:)`/`(commit:)`; :462-467 the 'These entries are tracked ... run annotate-pr' paragraph.
suggested_fix: Exclude entries with an active `(PR:)` or `(commit:)` from the injected fence and count them in the 'and N more' line. Drop or shorten the annotate paragraph.

summary: status.md says empty output means the repo has no open entries. In the current CLI a clean ledger prints `0 open`, and empty output means there is no ledger file.
failure_scenario: The agent runs `found-issues status --format=plain` in a repo with no ledger and no wired logging, gets empty output, and tells the user 'No open found-issues entries in this repo', which is misleading. For an existing clean ledger it gets `0 open`, a form status.md never lists.
evidence: status.md:16-17 'If the output is empty, the repo has no open entries.'; lib/list-status.sh:221-228 prints `0 open` when a ledger exists and is clean; empty only when no file.
suggested_fix: Document `0 open` as the clean-ledger output and say empty output means no ledger was found (run /found-issues:log to start one, or check cwd).
